name: Sony PlayStation 5 family
summary: Explore PS5 family hardware and firmware-specific routes into homebrew across original, Slim and Pro.

specs.gpu: Custom AMD RDNA graphics; original/Slim up to 10.3 TFLOPS, Pro 16.7 TFLOPS
specs.memory: 16 GB GDDR6; Pro adds 2 GB DDR5
specs.storage: Custom SSD; capacity varies by model
specs.media: UHD Blu-ray on disc editions; Digital editions have no drive, and Slim/Pro can use an optional paired drive

variants.notes: CFI-10xx, CFI-11xx and CFI-12xx model groups. Sold as a disc edition with an integrated UHD Blu-ray drive or Digital Edition without a drive.

specs.cpu: Custom AMD Zen 2, 8 cores / 16 threads, variable frequency up to 3.5 GHz
specs.gpu: Custom AMD RDNA 2, up to 2.23 GHz (10.3 TFLOPS)
specs.media: Integrated UHD Blu-ray drive on disc edition; Digital Edition has no drive

variants.storage: 1 TB on CFI-20xx; CFI-21xx: 1 TB disc edition / 825 GB Digital Edition
variants.notes: CFI-20xx Slim launched in 2023. Disc and Digital Editions exist; a detachable disc drive can be paired with compatible CFI-20xx/21xx Digital models.

specs.cpu: Custom AMD Zen 2, 8 cores / 16 threads, variable frequency up to 3.5 GHz
specs.gpu: Custom AMD RDNA 2, up to 2.23 GHz (10.3 TFLOPS)
specs.media: Disc model or Digital Edition; compatible detachable UHD Blu-ray drive

variants.notes: CFI-70xx/71xx model groups. Digital base console with 2 TB SSD; compatible detachable UHD Blu-ray drive is sold separately. The 30th Anniversary Limited Edition is also 2 TB, released November 21, 2024; its included disc-drive cover does not include the drive.

specs.media: Digital base console; compatible detachable UHD Blu-ray drive sold separately

homebrew.name: UMTX2
homebrew.firmware: Upstream states PS5 1.00–5.50 support and provides a separate offset file for each listed firmware revision.
homebrew.summary: A browser-based starting point for running unofficial code on an original PS5. It supports only the exact firmware revisions listed below.

compatibility.note: These exact revisions each have an upstream PS5 offset file. The repository does not publish separate Slim or Pro support.

requirements: PS5 on one of the listed firmware revisions.
A compatible WebKit route; upstream provides hosted pages and a media browser package.

homebrew.name: Relapse
homebrew.firmware: Exact upstream offsets are listed from 7.00 through 13.60, with gaps; Pro-specific coverage is not separately stated.
homebrew.summary: Uses the PS5 browser to start an exploit that can open deeper system access for unofficial apps. It may take retries, and a failure can freeze or crash the console.

compatibility.note: These are the exact firmware revisions represented by upstream Relapse offsets. The repository describes PS5 support but does not publish a separate original-versus-Slim matrix.
The upstream README lists PS5 firmware 7.00–13.60 but does not name Pro; Pro support is not stated.

requirements: PS5 on a firmware revision represented in the upstream offset list.
warnings: Upstream warns that retries may be needed and kernel-stage failures can hang or panic the console.

homebrew.name: Y2JB
homebrew.firmware: Upstream requires at least 4.03 and names backup packages for 4.03–12.40 and 12.60+; it does not publish an exact tested firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: Uses the YouTube app to start unofficial code, which can then load a separate kernel exploit. The project gives setup ranges but no exact tested firmware list.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes PS5 support and setup ranges, but does not list exact tested revisions or split original and Slim hardware.
The README requires a PS5 on 4.03 or newer and does not name Pro; Pro support is not stated.

requirements: PS5 system software 4.03 or newer.
Follow upstream account activation instructions; its fake-activation section requires a separate fake-activated account when a legit PSN account already exists.
For the non-jailbroken route, a USB drive and the matching pre-made system backup.
YouTube app package 01.000.003 for 4.03–12.40 or 01.000.030 for 12.60+ per upstream instructions.
warnings: Restoring the supplied system backup factory-resets the PS5 and erases console data; make a separate backup first.

homebrew.name: Y2JB + Lapse
homebrew.firmware: Y2JB describes the Lapse payload as working only up to 10.01. PSFree/Lapse lists PS5 vulnerability scope 1.00–10.01, but its current repository does not claim a tested PS5 chain.
homebrew.summary: A follow-on step for Y2JB that tries to open kernel-level access. The source gives a ceiling of 10.01, not a full list of working console and firmware combinations.

compatibility.note: The source gives a ceiling, not an exact tested revision list or original/Slim split.
Y2JB and PSFree/Lapse state a PS5 firmware ceiling only; neither names Pro.

requirements: Y2JB userland running on the console.
Firmware no higher than 10.01 per the Y2JB Lapse payload note.
A compatible payload receiver for the next ELF stage.

homebrew.name: P2JB (Y2JB chain)
homebrew.firmware: This community implementation lists 11.00, 11.20, 11.40, 11.60 and 12.00 as supported; 12.02+ offsets are unknown in this repo and 13.00+ is patched.
homebrew.summary: A kernel exploit loaded from Y2JB to open deeper system access. This implementation lists five firmware versions and has no separate PS5 Pro list.

compatibility.note: These exact revisions are listed by the implementation; its README says PS5 generically and does not split original from Slim.
The repository states PS5 firmware 11.00–12.00 and does not name Pro; Pro support is not stated.

requirements: Y2JB userland running on the console.
One of the exact firmware revisions listed by this implementation.
A compatible ELF loader on USB, as described by the project.
warnings: The project estimates roughly seven hours for the exploit run; this estimate is not a completion guarantee.

homebrew.name: Remote Lua Loader (save game)
homebrew.firmware: The project says the loader is not firmware-dependent and specifically reports a PS5 Pro test on 10.40; it gives no full exact firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: Runs Lua code from a supported game save as a way into unofficial code. It needs an activated PS5 account and a jailbroken PS4 to prepare the save; the project reports one PS5 Pro test on 10.40.

compatibility.note: Setup names PS5 and PS5 Slim, but the README gives no exact firmware test for those models.
The upstream README explicitly reports a PS5 Pro test on firmware 10.40; this is the only exact PS5 firmware test it names.

requirements: A previously PSN-activated PS5 account.
A jailbroken PS4 on firmware equal to or earlier than the PS5 firmware to prepare the save.
A game from the loader’s supported Artemis-engine list, installed on the PS5.
A matching save-data transfer from USB.
warnings: The setup replaces files in an exported game-save folder and imports modified save data; preserve an untouched copy of existing saves.

homebrew.name: BD-JB5
homebrew.firmware: The upstream entrypoint is documented through 13.42. At 13.60+ its BD-J unpatch step requires an already-jailbroken console, so it is not a first-entry route there.
homebrew.summary: Uses a prepared Blu-ray Java disc to run code through the PS5 disc player. The project documents it as an entry point through 13.42; on 13.60 and newer, it requires another jailbreak first.

compatibility.note: Upstream states support through 13.42 but does not publish exact firmware revisions or an original/Slim hardware matrix.
No Pro-specific support is stated.

requirements: A Blu-ray-capable PS5 and a BD-J disc carrying the project.
For 13.60 and newer, a separate working jailbreak and ELF loader are required before using bdj_unpatch.
warnings: Do not reinstall firmware after the 13.60+ BD-J unpatch; upstream says reinstalling removes the patch and loses BD-JB.

homebrew.name: PS5 Linux
homebrew.firmware: Original/Slim: exact listed versions. Pro: 13.60 only.
homebrew.summary: Boots Linux from an external USB drive so the PS5 can work like a small desktop PC. Firmware support differs by model; the Pro is listed only on 13.60.

compatibility.note: Upstream lists these exact Phat/Slim revisions; its README notes no M.2 support on 3.00–3.21.
Upstream lists 13.60 as the only supported Pro firmware.

requirements: A matching console/firmware combination from the exact matrix.
A working exploit/ELF loader, a USB drive of at least 64 GB and USB keyboard/mouse.
warnings: Linux boot conflicts with active etaHEN/kstuff; follow the Linux loader guide.
Writing the Linux image erases its target USB drive; ROMinit does not perform this operation.

homebrew.name: etaHEN (upstream)
homebrew.firmware: Release notes report 8.40–10.01 support fixes in 2.4B; exact current model/firmware matrix remains unverified. This is separate from the unofficial 11.00–13.60 port.
homebrew.summary: Adds a homebrew menu, plugins, optional FTP and Itemzflow features after a jailbreak. Upstream release notes mention fixes for 8.40–10.01; the exact current model and firmware list is not published.

compatibility.note: The upstream README and 2.4B release notes give no exact model/firmware matrix and do not name Pro.

requirements: A compatible exploit and Payload SDK ELF loader (required by upstream 2.4B release notes).

homebrew.name: kstuff-lite
homebrew.firmware: Release v1.11 lists firmware 1.00–13.60; it does not name Pro.
homebrew.summary: Adds kernel support that some homebrew and package features rely on after a compatible jailbreak. Support can vary by build; release v1.11 lists firmware 1.00–13.60.

compatibility.note: The v1.11 release states firmware 1.00–13.60 for PS5 without a model split.
The v1.11 release lists PS5 firmware but does not name Pro; Pro support is not stated.

requirements: A compatible jailbroken PS5 and a kstuff build matching its firmware.

homebrew.name: PS5 Payload SDK
homebrew.firmware: Development SDK for exploited PS5 systems; exact current firmware offsets were not verified.
homebrew.summary: A developer toolkit for building software that runs on PS5 as payloads. It does not provide a way into the console by itself; firmware support depends on the exploit and loader used.

compatibility.note: The README describes development for exploited PS5s but no exact supported firmware list.

homebrew.name: PS5 Payload ELF Loader
homebrew.firmware: Runs after a compatible jailbreak and bootstrap loader; the project does not publish an exact firmware list.
homebrew.summary: Lets a jailbroken PS5 receive and run ELF payload files from another tool. It needs a compatible bootstrap loader, and the project does not list exact firmware support.

compatibility.note: Upstream documents prerequisites and behavior but no exact firmware/model matrix.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with a compatible ELF loading path.

homebrew.name: Itemzflow
homebrew.firmware: PS5 support is listed upstream; exact firmware/model compatibility is not published in the reviewed README.
homebrew.summary: A homebrew game manager with an alternate home menu and a PS5 game compatibility list. It needs a compatible jailbreak; the project does not list exact firmware support.

compatibility.note: The README links PS5 game compatibility information but does not specify a firmware/model support matrix.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 and compatible homebrew environment.

homebrew.name: etaHEN 2.5B Unified r1 (unofficial port)
homebrew.firmware: Exact release profiles: 11.00–13.60 with gaps; 11.40 excluded. Hardware-specific testing is not established here.
homebrew.summary: A community port of etaHEN that adds a menu, plugins, an FPS display and bundled kstuff-lite. Its release lists firmware profiles with gaps and no separate Pro support list.

compatibility.note: The release publishes exact PS5 profiles; this records project claims, not testing of each console revision.
This release does not publish a separate Pro validation matrix.

requirements: A compatible jailbreak and ELF loader after a fresh boot.
warnings: Do not load over an existing etaHEN instance.
Includes kstuff-lite: do not load a second kstuff copy.

homebrew.name: Byepervisor Reborn
homebrew.firmware: Upstream fully supports 13.20 and 13.60; 13.00 is listed as untested. The broader 6.xx–13.60 vulnerability span is not the implemented support list.
homebrew.summary: A developer research payload for exploring PS5 hypervisor access, below the normal kernel layer. It needs kernel access and elfldr; upstream lists 13.20 and 13.60 as supported and 13.00 as untested.

compatibility.note: Upstream documents Pro and non-Pro units; main.c detects a Pro unit and uses the Pro hypervisor physical address. Supported firmware is 13.20 and 13.60.
Upstream labels 13.00 untested; no claim for every firmware affected by the underlying bug.

requirements: An already working kernel exploit chain and elfldr.
Rest Mode USB power configured as required by upstream.
warnings: Developer base exploit: does not include HEN or other patches.
Rest Mode/resume failure can shut down the console.

homebrew.name: PS5 Payload Web Server
homebrew.firmware: Requires an exploited PS5 and running ELF loader; exact firmware/model matrix not published.
homebrew.summary: Adds a web page for launching homebrew and browsing files on the PS5. It needs an exploited console and a running ELF loader.

compatibility.note: The project documents a BD-J/WebKit prerequisite rather than an exact firmware matrix.

requirements: A compatible jailbreak and ps5-payload-elfldr already running.
warnings: Upstream notes that launching homebrew while another homebrew is running can crash.

homebrew.name: ezRemote Client
homebrew.firmware: Requires websrv; the project does not publish an exact PS5 firmware/model matrix.
homebrew.summary: A PS5 file manager for connecting to FTP, SFTP, SMB, NFS, WebDAV and HTTP servers. It needs websrv and a working homebrew setup.

compatibility.note: Application prerequisites are documented; firmware support must be checked through the selected jailbreak, loader and websrv build.

requirements: An exploited PS5 with the websrv payload running.
The application files installed under /data/homebrew as described upstream.
warnings: Background downloads do not continue through Rest Mode.
Upstream warns that too many queued background installs can crash ezRemote Server.

compatibility.note: This host-side tool does not establish console firmware compatibility.

warnings: Writing an image erases the target drive. Double-check the selected device.
homebrew.name: balenaEtcher
homebrew.firmware: USB media preparation; does not flash PS5 system firmware.
homebrew.summary: Writes a Linux image to a USB drive for booting PS5 Linux, then checks that the write completed. It runs on a computer and does not install PS5 system software.
requirements: A supported PS5 Linux image and a suitable external drive (upstream requires at least 64 GB).

compatibility.note: This host-side tool does not establish console firmware compatibility.

homebrew.name: Hermes Link
homebrew.firmware: Network payload sender; not a USB firmware flasher or an initial jailbreak.
homebrew.summary: Sends payload data over a network to a PS5 that already has a compatible loader running. It needs that network loader and does not prepare USB media.
requirements: A working exploit and payload loader on the PS5.
A matching payload and correct network address/port.

homebrew.name: RetroArch for PS5
homebrew.firmware: Requires a working PS5 homebrew environment; the project does not publish an app-specific firmware compatibility matrix.
homebrew.summary: One app for using emulators for older consoles and computers on a PS5 homebrew setup. The project lists 33 built cores for 44 systems; which games run depends on the core.
homebrew.systems: Multi-system: NES, Game Boy family, SNES, N64, GameCube/Wii, DS/3DS, PS1/PS2/PSP, Sega consoles, arcade, home computers, and more.

compatibility.note: Project requires a compatible jailbreak and launcher; no project-specific firmware or model test matrix is published.

requirements: Compatible PS5 jailbreak and homebrew launcher.
ShadowMountPlus 1.7 beta 4 or later is recommended for USB and extended-storage access.
warnings: Alpha software; core and game compatibility varies.
No games, BIOS files, console firmware, or decryption keys are bundled; use your own legally obtained dumps.
homebrew.availability: Published alpha build; upstream lists supported systems.

homebrew.name: PS5SX2
homebrew.firmware: Upstream-reported tests: PS5 Pro 10.01 and 11.40; non-Pro PS5 models, including Slim, 6.02, 8.40, 10.01, 10.60, 11.40, 11.60, 12.00, and 12.70. These are test reports, not a guarantee.
homebrew.summary: Runs PlayStation 2 games in a native PS5 port of PCSX2. The developers publish console and firmware test reports; versions outside their table are not covered by those reports.

compatibility.note: Project reports PS5 Pro tests on these firmware versions
Project reports non-Pro PS5 tests, including Slim, on these firmware versions

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and the PS5SX2 Helper payload, plus ShadowMountPlus or the documented title-launch method.
A PS2 BIOS and game dumps supplied by the user.
warnings: Game results vary and can regress between builds.
No BIOS, games, or keys are bundled.

links.label: Source, test matrix, and game compatibility

homebrew.availability: Published build; upstream reports tests on the listed model and firmware pairs.

homebrew.name: PSXS5
homebrew.firmware: The project says development happens on firmware 13.60; it does not publish a broader tested firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: Runs PlayStation 1 games in a native PS5 app with Beetle PSX HW and PCSX-ReARMed cores. It can choose a core per game and includes saves, Vulkan graphics and RetroAchievements.

compatibility.note: Firmware 13.60 is the stated development environment, not a published support matrix.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with etaHEN and kstuff, plus ShadowMountPlus or the documented helper route.
PS1 games supplied by the user; an optional PS1 BIOS improves compatibility.
warnings: Hobby project; expect rough edges and title-specific compatibility differences.
No games or BIOS files are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build; upstream describes a native PS1 app.

homebrew.name: SwanStationPS5
homebrew.firmware: The project says development happens on firmware 13.60; it does not publish a broader tested firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: Runs PlayStation 1 games in a standalone PS5 app based on SwanStation. It can share PSXS5 game and BIOS folders so both apps use the same files.

compatibility.note: Firmware 13.60 is the stated development environment, not a published support matrix.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with etaHEN and kstuff, plus ShadowMountPlus.
PS1 game dumps; the built-in OpenBIOS is available, while a user-supplied BIOS may improve compatibility.
warnings: Separate PS1 app that overlaps with PSXS5; it is not a new system-compatibility tier.
No games or copyrighted BIOS files are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build; upstream describes a native PS1 app.

homebrew.name: PSP5
homebrew.firmware: No project-specific firmware range is published; requires a working PS5 homebrew environment.
homebrew.summary: A standalone PS5 app for emulating PSP games, based on PPSSPP. The repository has source code but no downloadable release package.

compatibility.note: No project-specific firmware or model test matrix is published.

requirements: A working PS5 homebrew environment and a title launcher.
A jailbreak service that grants folder listing for USB game libraries; otherwise games must be in the title's own folder.
warnings: The repository has no GitHub release listed; treat it as a source project requiring a build.
No PSP games or system files are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Source-only; repository has no GitHub release package.

homebrew.name: PS5-ECAM
homebrew.firmware: The project says any firmware up to 13.60 where the console can run homebrew; the firmware entry point and HEN remain firmware-dependent.
homebrew.summary: An all-in-one app for emulating Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, Nintendo DS and Switch games. It bundles Cemu, Azahar, melonDS and Eden through ProsperoEden; the latest listed release is 5.0.0.
homebrew.systems: Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, Nintendo DS, Nintendo Switch

compatibility.note: Project setup guide describes any firmware up to 13.60 if homebrew can be loaded; model-specific compatibility is not published.

requirements: A PS5 that can run homebrew with etaHEN, OnionHEN, or an ELF loader on port 9021.
For Switch, user-supplied game keys and firmware are required; each system needs user-owned game dumps.
warnings: Game compatibility and performance vary by emulator and title.
PS5CEMU-HAR was renamed to PS5-ECAM; do not list the legacy app as a separate current project.
No games, keys, or firmware are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build (5.0.0); setup and firmware ceiling are upstream-reported.

homebrew.name: ProsperoEden
homebrew.firmware: Requires a working PS5 homebrew environment; the project does not publish a complete supported-firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: A native PS5 app for Nintendo Switch emulation, also used inside PS5-ECAM. The project labels it early alpha and asks testers to report their console and system software.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes an early alpha and asks testers to report model and system software; no full matrix is published.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 and the title-launch/elevation setup documented by the project.
User-supplied Switch games, keys, and firmware.
warnings: Early alpha; video, audio, controller input, and saves are reported working, but game compatibility and performance vary.
No Switch games, keys, or firmware are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published early-alpha build; upstream asks testers to report model and system software.

homebrew.name: Porpoise-X
homebrew.firmware: The project documents user reports on firmware 13.60 and does not publish a complete model/firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: Uses Dolphin to emulate GameCube and Wii games on PS5, with a game library and per-game settings. Wii support and motion-heavy controls are marked experimental.
homebrew.systems: Nintendo GameCube, Wii, WiiWare, Virtual Console, and Wii channels

compatibility.note: Project documents user reports for selected jailbreaks on 13.60; no complete model matrix is published.

requirements: A PS5 that can run homebrew, with a supported jailbreak/HEN and title launcher; ShadowMountPlus 1.7 beta 4 or newer is recommended.
User-owned GameCube/Wii game dumps.
warnings: Wii support and motion-heavy controls are experimental; per-game performance varies.
No games, BIOS, or firmware are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build; upstream lists selected firmware 13.60 reports.

homebrew.name: Castation
homebrew.firmware: Only the authors' console and loader combinations are reported tested; firmware versions and broader model support are not published.
homebrew.summary: Runs Dreamcast games in a native PS5 app based on Flycast. It reads common disc-image formats; the project notes current speed and graphics limits.

compatibility.note: Authors report testing on their own consoles; other firmware and loader combinations are unverified.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with a homebrew environment and Homebrew Launcher.
User-owned Dreamcast disc images; a BIOS is optional because HLE BIOS is available.
warnings: Reported emulation speed is about 96% of full speed, with occasional shader/JIT hitches and slowdowns in demanding scenes.
No games or BIOS files are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build; authors report hardware testing, but model and firmware are unspecified.

homebrew.name: PS5X360
homebrew.firmware: Development setup reports firmware 13.60; other firmware/model setups are unverified. The latest 0.6.0 package was not itself opened on a console before publication.
homebrew.summary: An experimental PS5 port of Xenia Canary for Xbox 360 games, with Vulkan graphics, audio and DualSense input. Game compatibility varies, and release 0.6.0 was not itself tested on a console.

compatibility.note: Project reports development on firmware 13.60 but does not provide a complete model matrix; latest package was not console-tested as a release.

requirements: A working PS5 homebrew environment, including the documented jailbreak, kstuff, and title launcher setup.
Xbox 360 game files supplied by the user; no Xbox 360 BIOS is required by the project.
warnings: Experimental; crashes, visual errors, uneven performance, and title-specific failures are expected.
The latest package release is not a fresh hardware acceptance test; use its release notes for evidence limits.
Release notes state the v0.6.0 package was not opened on a console before publication; earlier development tests do not validate this exact build.
homebrew.availability: Published build (0.6.0); release states this package was not itself console-tested, hardware validation incomplete.

homebrew.name: XPSemu
homebrew.firmware: The project reports testing on a PS5 Fat but does not publish its firmware version or a broader model matrix.
homebrew.summary: An experimental native PS5 app for original Xbox games, based on xemu. The Alpha 2 report says it boots and runs selected games on a PS5 Fat; game support varies.

compatibility.note: Upstream reports Alpha 2 tests on a PS5 Fat; firmware is not stated.
No model-specific test evidence was found.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with the required helper payload and ShadowMountPlus.
User-dumped original Xbox system files and games.
warnings: Alpha; performance and compatibility vary, and some games remain slow or incomplete.
No BIOS, games, or keys are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published alpha build; upstream reports tests on a PS5 Fat, with firmware unspecified.

homebrew.name: rpcs3-PS5
homebrew.firmware: The repository reports a PS5 Pro test on firmware 13.60; no other console/firmware combinations are documented.
homebrew.summary: An early native PS5 port of RPCS3 for PlayStation 3 games. The developer reports Need for Speed Carbon playable in one PS5 Pro test on 13.60; this is source code, not an official RPCS3 release.

compatibility.note: The repository reports this single-console test
No model-specific test evidence was found.

requirements: A PS5 homebrew environment; building requires a Linux/Arch-like development host, the PS5 payload toolchain, and about 20 GB of disk space.
User-supplied PS3 firmware and game dumps.
warnings: Source only and personal use only; the repository says built title binaries must not be redistributed because of its license mix.
Experimental, with crashes and freezes expected; most games are untested.
homebrew.availability: Source-only; no GitHub release/package. Developer reports one PS5 Pro test on 13.60.

homebrew.name: KB-RPCS3
homebrew.firmware: No supported firmware or model matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: A separate early project to run RPCS3 as a native PS5 app for PlayStation 3 games. Alpha 0.1.0 is source code only, and its release says the combined executable has not passed final PS5 testing.

compatibility.note: No model/firmware hardware compatibility matrix was found.

requirements: A working PS5 homebrew environment and a source build using the documented PS5 toolchain.
warnings: Alpha source release; no downloadable PS5 package is available, and the project identifies an unresolved license mix that prevents binary distribution.
Expect crashes; no games or firmware are bundled.
Do not present as an installable emulator: its release contains source and checksums, not a PS5 title package.
homebrew.availability: Source-only alpha; release has no PS5 package and says the combined executable has not passed final PS5 testing.

homebrew.name: Vita3K for PS5
homebrew.firmware: No project-specific PS5 firmware or model compatibility matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: An experimental PS5 port of Vita3K for PlayStation Vita games, with a controller-driven interface. Its README says games can run, while the porting plan still lists the first hardware boot as pending.

compatibility.note: No firmware/model matrix is published, and the README conflicts with the porting plan about hardware validation.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with the PS5SX2 Helper, kstuff, and ShadowMountPlus, as documented by the project.
User-provided Vita firmware, game files, and required licenses.
warnings: No games, firmware, or licenses are bundled.

Experimental alpha package. README claims games boot and run, but the porting plan still lists first hardware boot as an acceptance task; resolve this source conflict before describing it as hardware-validated.
homebrew.availability: Published alpha package (PPSA99300.zip); README claims games run, while porting plan still lists first hardware boot as pending.

homebrew.name: Ruffle Flash PS5
homebrew.firmware: Requires a jailbroken PS5 with kstuff and a helper; no project-specific firmware matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: Runs Flash games and animations in a native PS5 app using Ruffle, an open-source Flash Player emulator. It supports ActionScript 1, 2 and 3.

compatibility.note: No project-specific firmware or model test matrix is published.

requirements: A jailbroken PS5 with kstuff, a helper payload, and ShadowMountPlus.
User-provided SWF files.
warnings: Compatibility follows Ruffle and varies by content; H.264 Flash video is unsupported and demanding ActionScript 3 games can run slowly.
No SWF content is bundled.
homebrew.availability: Published build; upstream lists Flash feature support.

homebrew.name: EmuC0re
homebrew.firmware: Project claims support on PS5 firmware up to 13.00 through LuaC0re; it does not claim later firmware support.
homebrew.summary: A proof-of-concept NES emulator that runs as a small userland payload through LuaC0re, without a kernel exploit. The source claims support through firmware 13.00 and lists supported NES mappers.

compatibility.note: Project claims firmware support up to 13.00 and requires LuaC0re; model-specific tests are not listed.

requirements: LuaC0re and the documented PS2 game trigger (Star Wars Racer Revenge, US CUSA03474 or EU CUSA03492).
A PC on the same network to send the payload and upload user-provided NES ROMs.
warnings: Proof of concept; games using unsupported NES mappers will not run.
No games are bundled.

links.label: Source, firmware claim, and mapper support

homebrew.availability: Source-only userland payload; the firmware ceiling is a project claim.

homebrew.name: LuaGB
homebrew.firmware: Requires LuaC0re; the project does not publish a PS5 firmware range.
homebrew.summary: A Game Boy and Game Boy Color emulator that runs as shellcode through LuaC0re. It uses the fixGB core and reads games and saves from savedata; the project gives no PS5 firmware range.
homebrew.systems: Nintendo Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Sound System

compatibility.note: No project-specific firmware or model test matrix is published.

requirements: LuaC0re set up with its loader, Star Wars Racer Revenge (US CUSA03474 or EU CUSA03492), and a PC on the same network.
ROMs must be placed in the game's savedata container as documented.
warnings: Small source project; no formal release or compatibility matrix is published.
No games are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Source-only project; no formal release or firmware matrix.

homebrew.name: AnyPS5
homebrew.firmware: Runs on a Linux or Windows PC, not on the console; firmware of the source console does not apply.
homebrew.summary: Ports PS5 game and app executables to Linux and Windows. It relinks the executable against its own system library implementations and recompiles shaders to Vulkan, with no emulator or separate runtime process. A web converter runs in the browser and keeps files on your device.
homebrew.runtime: Relinked native executable on Linux or Windows (Vulkan); relinker-only build on macOS
requirements: Your own legally obtained app dump: one executable ELF plus its sce_sys/ and sce_module/ folders
A Linux or Windows PC with a Vulkan GPU
A controller via SDL (mapping in anyps5-input.ini)
warnings: Early 0.1.x release: many games are blocked; check the community blocker map before converting.
AnyPS5 bundles no firmware or keys; dumping your own games needs a jailbroken console.
homebrew.availability: Release v0.1.3, published 2026-10-20 · GPL-2.0

homebrew.name: PS5 Linux (emulation host)
homebrew.summary: Boots Linux from USB, then lets you install desktop emulators on the PS5. This is a way to run Linux emulators, not a native PS5 emulator; the model and firmware list is below.
homebrew.systems: Linux emulators installed separately from the selected distribution; no emulator is bundled with this project.

compatibility.note: Firmware list is from the upstream loader README. M.2 support is unavailable on 3.00–3.21
Upstream lists PS5 Pro 13.60 only

requirements: A supported PS5 firmware/model combination, the PS5-Linux loader, a USB boot drive, and Linux peripherals as documented.
A Linux distribution image; install any emulator packages separately.
warnings: This is a Linux host path, not a native PS5 emulator and not a promise that every desktop emulator package or game works.
Requires re-running the exploit to boot Linux; project does not support firmware 14.00 or higher.
homebrew.availability: Linux host, not an emulator; loader and distro images are published with an upstream firmware list.

homebrew.name: PS5 firmware rollback status — no verified general method
homebrew.firmware: No general rollback firmware support established
homebrew.summary: Records the documented PS5 downgrade limit: the sources say an older system PUP will not install, and no general rollback method is documented. This is a status reference, not a downgrade tool.

compatibility.note: No PS5 model-specific rollback method was verified; the installation guide says lower-version PUPs do not install.

warnings: An archived older PUP is not a downgrade method. Sony reinstall/update and PS4 revert procedures must not be presented as PS5 rollback.
Any isolated rollback claim needs independent, reproducible confirmation before being treated as usable.

homebrew.name: Sony PS5 system software update and reinstall
homebrew.firmware: Latest official system software: 26.07-14.20.00, checked on Sony's features page. Update and reinstall files are different.
homebrew.summary: Sony’s official instructions for updating PS5 from USB or reinstalling system software in Safe Mode. Reinstalling erases console data; it does not provide an older-firmware selector.

compatibility.note: Official PS5 recovery/update track, shared by the PS5 family; not a claim that reinstall accepts older firmware.

requirements: FAT32- or exFAT-formatted USB drive with PS5/UPDATE/PS5UPDATE.PUP; use Safe Mode as Sony documents.
warnings: Sony says system software reinstallation deletes all PS5 data.
Sony warns an interrupted installation can damage the console and recommends official Sony update data and documented methods.

homebrew.name: Darthsternie's PS5 firmware archive
homebrew.firmware: Historical system and recovery PUP archive; not an authority for the current release or proof of downgrade support.
homebrew.summary: A third-party archive of historical PS5 update and recovery PUP files with checksums. An older file in the archive does not make a PS5 downgrade possible.

compatibility.note: The archive does not give a CFI model compatibility matrix or a downgrade bypass.

warnings: This is a third-party archive, not Sony. Its listed MD5 values are not a substitute for independent authenticity checks.
Historical PUPs do not enable downgrading; follow the official Sony install path only when its version checks accept the package.
The recovery PUP reinstall path erases console data.

homebrew.name: Luac0re
homebrew.firmware: Version 2.0 adds a JIT exploit for userland code on then-latest PS4/PS5 firmware without a kernel exploit; its Poopsploit payload is limited to PS5 12.00 or lower.
homebrew.summary: A mast1c0re variation that uses the Lua interpreter in Star Wars Racer Revenge to run native userland code on PS4 and PS5. It needs no kernel exploit, but it also gives no kernel access.

compatibility.note: Project claims userland code execution on the latest firmware at release, but names 12.00 as the Poopsploit ceiling; no model or firmware matrix is published.

requirements: A disc or digital copy of Star Wars Racer Revenge, US CUSA03474 or EU CUSA03492.
The project savedata, resigned with the remote_lua_loader setup guide.
warnings: Userland only: it does not provide kernel access, and the project describes the JIT route as an exploit-development aid.
The Poopsploit payload is capped at PS5 firmware 12.00.
No game files are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

entrypoints.note: An entry point is the first way to run community-made code on your console. Different routes use different apps, discs or browser features, and only work on certain firmware versions.

models.note: Chips show the firmware each layer is documented for by the projects below. Firmware lists have gaps; check your exact version in the route finder. Updating past these versions closes the route.

finder.help: Pick the model and firmware shown in your console settings. The box below links to every project that lists your model, documented ones first. Open each project’s setup notes for the apps or equipment you need.
finder.note: Documented means the project names this model and firmware. "Firmware not confirmed" projects list your model without an exact firmware list: check their notes first. These are first steps, not a complete jailbreak setup. All projects remain listed below.

linux.title: Run Linux on your PS5
linux.note: Linux turns the console into a desktop-like computer for compatible software and emulators. You need a supported jailbreak route and usually a separate USB drive.

emulation.note: Emulators let your PS5 play games made for other systems. Some run as PS5 homebrew; others need Linux installed first. The systems and setup needed are listed on each card. Performance varies by game.

pc.title: Play PS5 games on other devices
pc.link: Play PS5 games on other devices ↓
pc.note: The reverse of the section above: instead of other systems on your PS5, your PS5 games on a computer, such as AnyPS5. These tools convert games you dumped from your own console. Nothing is installed on the PS5, but dumping a game needs a jailbroken console first.

tools.note: A USB image writer prepares a drive; a payload sender uses an existing loader. Neither is automatically a PS5 firmware flasher.
